Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co Announces Major Expansion Project in Zarqa

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, the kingdom’s leading oil and gas producer, has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its refining capacity at its flagship facility in Zarqa. The investment, valued at over $2 billion, is set to enhance the refinery’s output and efficiency, aligning with Jordan’s broader economic development goals and energy security strategy.

The expansion project, which will be implemented in phases over the next four years, aims to boost the refinery’s capacity from the current 60,000 barrels per day to approximately 120,000 barrels per day. According to company officials, the new facilities will incorporate advanced technologies designed to improve fuel quality, reduce emissions, and optimize energy consumption.

Speaking at a press briefing on Tuesday, Samer Al-Nawas, CEO of Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co, emphasized the strategic importance of the project. “This expansion is a milestone for both the company and the national economy. It will reduce Jordan’s reliance on imported refined products, create hundreds of new jobs, and further position the kingdom as a regional energy hub,” Al-Nawas said.

The expansion comes amid rising domestic demand for refined petroleum products, driven by robust growth in the transportation, industrial, and power generation sectors. Industry analysts have welcomed the move, noting that it aligns with the government’s ambitions to foster local industry and reduce the trade deficit.

Fadi Khalil, an energy analyst at Amman-based consultancy Petra Insights, commented, “Upgrading the Zarqa refinery is a logical step given the country’s growing consumption and the need for cleaner, more efficient fuel. The investment also signals confidence in Jordan’s long-term economic outlook.”

In addition to increasing capacity, the project will introduce new units for the production of higher-grade gasoline and diesel, in line with Euro V standards. Environmental considerations are central to the expansion, with the company pledging to deploy state-of-the-art emissions control systems and improve waste management processes.

The Jordanian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources has expressed support for the project, citing its potential to stimulate local supply chains and provide training opportunities for Jordanian engineers and technicians. Construction is expected to begin in early 2025, with full commissioning scheduled for late 2028.

Jordan Petroleum Refinery Co has indicated that a consortium of local and international engineering firms, including the Amman-based Al-Hilal Engineering, will be involved in the design and implementation. The company is also exploring financing options with regional banks and multilateral institutions to ensure the timely delivery of the project.
